newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Purneftegaz oil firm court case delayed.
newsitem.headline: Russian Purneftegaz oil firm court case delayed.

text.p: Russia's Supreme Court has delayed a hearing on the ownership of Russian oil firm Purneftegaz, in a move which may push back the privatisation of the Rosneft oil holding company, which claims the producer.
Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Vyunitsky said on Thursday a hearing set for August 15 had been pushed back by at least three weeks over procedural matters.
The hearing, which would resolve one of Russia's longest-standing and closely watched corporate ownership disputes, could take place September 6, Vyunitsky said.
Rosneft and rival oil group SIDANKO, one of whose main production units is Chernogorneft, both claim ownership of AO Purneftegaz.
The decision on who owns the producer will affect the privatisation of Rosneft, of which 51 percent is to be sold through a special cash auction, probably in September.

Purneftegaz was part of state-owned Rosneft but was then transferred under sweeping industry restructuring to SIDANKO. Various court decisions have awarded the company back to Rosneft or confirmed SIDANKO's ownership. The next decision will be the final one.
